title: Dalton Caldwell: Build startups that create more wealth than they capture
summary: Dalton and PB of Standard Capital explain how wealth is created (positive-sum exchange, marketplaces, better decisions) and why founders should know exactly where their startup creates it. Dalton's advice: make customers far better off than you, and capture only a slice of the value you create.

principles.text: Know exactly how your startup creates wealth for users and customers; the more, the better.
principles.quote: you should understand how your startup is creating wealth. And the more wealth you create for your users and your customers, the better.

principles.text: Create more value than you capture, and be clear on where the wealth is created.
principles.quote: our advice is to create more value than you capture and have a really good idea on where the wealth is being created by your startup.

principles.text: Test for wealth creation by comparing the value customers get against what the startup itself gets.
principles.quote: I like to think about how much value the customers of a startup are getting versus the startup itself to know if they're making wealth.

principles.text: Being slightly cheaper than a competitor is not value creation; be far better than the alternatives.
principles.quote: it's creating value not necessarily because you're the lowest cost solution versus a competitor. It's that you're so much better than other options.

principles.text: Real wealth creation is positive-sum: you add value without cheating or stealing from anyone.
principles.quote: you didn't cheat anyone, you didn't steal, you you put labor into an action and it created more value than what the labor was worth.

principles.text: Sort ideas by whether they are positive-sum and create wealth; the real question is which bucket a startup falls in.
principles.quote: We just have a different criteria about who's in the bucket of positive sum things that create wealth and who's not.
